scenes.title: Four parts. Forty questions.
scenes.text: Welcome to Listening. You will hear four recordings and answer forty questions. Each recording plays once.

scenes.title: Read, listen and answer
scenes.text: Read the questions before each recording. Type your answers or select an option while you listen.

scenes.title: Follow the word limit
scenes.text: Follow each question's word limit. Check your spelling, and use the question numbers to navigate.

scenes.title: Two minutes to check
scenes.text: After the final recording, you have two minutes to check your answers. Your test then submits automatically.

scenes.title: Three passages. Sixty minutes.
scenes.text: Welcome to Academic Reading. You have sixty minutes to read three passages and answer forty questions.

scenes.title: Read and answer side by side
scenes.text: Read the passage on the left and answer on the right. Scroll each panel to find information.

scenes.title: Move between questions
scenes.text: Use the question numbers to move between answers. Follow the instructions and word limits carefully.

scenes.title: Check before time expires
scenes.text: Manage your time across all three passages. Check your answers before the timer ends. There is no extra transfer time.

scenes.title: Two tasks. Sixty minutes.
scenes.text: Welcome to Academic Writing. You have sixty minutes to complete both tasks. Type your responses in the answer areas.

scenes.title: Task 1 · at least 150 words
scenes.text: For Task One, describe the visual information in at least one hundred and fifty words. Allow about twenty minutes.

scenes.title: Task 2 · at least 250 words
scenes.text: For Task Two, write an essay of at least two hundred and fifty words. Allow about forty minutes.

scenes.title: Task 2 carries twice the weight
scenes.text: Task Two carries twice the weight of Task One. Use the word counter and check both responses before time expires.

scenes.title: Three parts. One conversation.
scenes.text: Welcome to Speaking. This practice uses an AI examiner. The real IELTS interview is conducted by a human examiner.

scenes.title: Part 1 · familiar topics
scenes.text: Check your microphone. In Part One, answer questions about familiar topics, such as your studies, work, or interests.

scenes.title: Part 2 · your long turn
scenes.text: In Part Two, you have one minute to prepare. Then speak about the cue card for up to two minutes.

scenes.title: Part 3 · develop your ideas
scenes.text: In Part Three, discuss broader ideas related to the topic. Speak clearly, extend your answers, and explain your opinions.
